_note: How a pack has to be read, when reading it as it ships would be wrong. Keyed by the kit folder name in BabylonAssets/kits. A kit that is not named here is loaded exactly as it comes, which is the case for every glTF kit.

Ultimate Nature Pack._why: Quaternius' .fbx packs are exported with every face flat: all 1450 vertices of CommonTree_1 carry as many normals as they have corners, up to 159 degrees apart. Their own renders are smooth-shaded, and a faceted trunk next to a smooth-shaded ship reads as broken rather than as stylised.

Ultimate RPG Items Pack._why: Same export, same fix. 60 degrees keeps a sword's bevels and its blade-to-guard corner hard - those edges are 75 degrees and over - while rounding the shaft and pommel facets, which sit at 45.

materials._why: Glass and the five liquids are the only materials in the pack that reach Babylon with no colour at all - 53 of them, against 214 that carry one. They are exactly the see-through ones: Blender's FBX exporter writes Phong properties from a Principled BSDF and has nothing to write for a transparent shader, so it wrote no property block, and Babylon fell back on its default 0.8 grey. That is why a filled potion looked identical to an empty one - the liquid, the glass and nothing at all were all the same colour.
materials._values: The pack's own palette, taken from the opaque material of the matching hue and multiplied by the 0.8 DiffuseFactor the loader applies to those, so a red potion is the same red as a red gem. Yellow has no opaque twin; LightGold is the pack's nearest.
